identity.title: Stratified gradient Hamiltonian vector fields and collective integrable systems
identity.journal: Journal of the European Mathematical Society

actual_source_version.limitation: Exact pinned author manuscript; publisher PDF unavailable through the normal public link. Differences from publisher text have not been compared.

findings.title: The specified Rees filtration need not be additive
findings.decisive_evidence: C[x,y], lex maximum exponent, w=id, K={x,y}, J=0, e(a,b)=a+b; x and -x+y^2 have degree one but sum y^2 has degree two. All v1–v5 hold. Secondary formal/evaluated degree defect checked with K={x,y,x^2+y}.
findings.alternative: Interpreting displayed value as formal degree repairs the secondary formula, not the independent failure of additivity.
findings.impact: Invalid general construction used by Proposition 4.13 and Theorems 4.16,5.5; does not prove nonexistence of collective systems.
findings.repair_status: Only local formal-degree correction checked; full filtration repair unverified

independent_verification.source_scope: PDF pp.19-21; Definition 4.1, (v1)-(v5), Lemma 4.4 and (14)-(16); dependency pp.24-27,33. Pinned author TeX lines 919-954 corroborates the displayed expressions.
independent_verification.hypotheses: For the first witness, the max-lex valuation on C[x,y] has one-dimensional leaves, saturated finitely generated value semigroup N^2 generating Z^2; w=id is onto, descends the order, has least value 0 and finite singleton fibers; homogeneous elements are scalar monomials. Strict same-w comparisons in (v5) do not arise. The identity embedding and K={x,y} give J=0, so e(a,b)=a+b satisfies every imposed restriction.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Independently derived and computed e(v(x))=e(v(-x+y^2))=1 but e(v(y^2))=2. This refutes the asserted additive subspace for allowed data. In the secondary witness, order=(a+2b,a), w=a+2b, K={x,y,x^2+y}; e=2a+2b is nonnegative and strictly refines every same-w comparison. Both evaluated relation and correction have value (0,1), while formal relation degree is (2,0).
independent_verification.counterevidence: Using formal degree fixes the secondary inequality, and the specific corrected t^2 binomial vanishes exactly under the indicated substitution. That does not repair the independent nonadditivity example. No unstated restriction to homogeneous f occurs in the displayed set definition.
independent_verification.impact: Retain Major for an invalid construction explicitly invoked by Proposition 4.13 (proof p.25), Theorems 4.16 and 5.5, and Section 6. No nonexistence result and no complete replacement filtration are asserted.
independent_verification.repair_check: Local formal-degree identity verified exactly; a general repaired construction remains unverified.

findings.title: Smooth-locus identification fails for constructed open set at positive complexity
findings.decisive_evidence: T^3 acting on CP6 with weights 0, ±e1, ±e2, ±e3. Construction yields U=D=Y; moment image octahedron has four facets at e1 and is not smooth there.
findings.alternative: Smaller invariant open set may recover existential statement; no refutation of convexity or connected fibers.
findings.impact: Main proof's identification is invalid; main theorem as existential claim not disproved
findings.repair_status: Restriction works in counterexample only; general repair not established

independent_verification.source_scope: PDF p.7 Section 2.2; pp.36-41 construction and Proposition 6.10(iii); p.3 Theorem 1.1(C).
independent_verification.hypotheses: K=T^3 is compact connected; CP6 is compact connected smooth with invariant Fubini-Study form. The diagonal weights 0,+/-e1,+/-e2,+/-e3 define an effective Hamiltonian action. Compactness supplies the properness required in Proposition 6.10. There is no multiplicity-free hypothesis. The torus has one Weyl stratum equal to its full dual Lie algebra.
independent_verification.decisive_check: For trivial semisimple factor, X=U^sigma=T*T^3, c=F=id; implosion is unchanged and the free cotangent translation makes the reduced space canonically Y, with U=D=Y. The weighted projective moment map realizes every convex combination of its weights. Independent exact facet calculation gives four genuine facets at e1 in dimension three; the vertex is nonsimple and hence not smooth in the source's rational-polyhedral sense.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The zero weight ensures effectiveness. Positive complexity (6-3=3) permits a nonsmooth image for a smooth Hamiltonian manifold. The smooth-toric-manifold theorem does not apply. A smaller invariant open set works in this example; that possibility does not validate the printed equality for the specified U.
independent_verification.impact: Retain Major for the false constructed-set identification explicitly used by the proof of Theorem 1.1 on p.41. Convexity, connected fibers, and existential availability of another domain are not refuted.
independent_verification.repair_check: Example-level restriction only; no general connectedness or replacement-construction theorem claimed.

findings.title: Missing necessary toric binomial in Example 4.17
findings.decisive_evidence: v1+v6=v2+v4; point (1,0,0,0,0,1) satisfies printed pair but y1*y6-y2*y4=1.
findings.alternative: A saturated torus-chart reading differs from the displayed affine set.
findings.impact: Illustrative affine variety wrong; example expressly unused later
findings.repair_status: Necessary binomial proved; sufficient full ideal not claimed

independent_verification.source_scope: PDF pp.27-29, Example 4.17 and (21); pinned TeX lines 1292-1295.
independent_verification.hypotheses: The source gives an affine set equality in E=C6 and identifies its ideal with the kernel of the displayed semigroup map. The six generators in the report match the source.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Independently checked v1+v6=v2+v4=(1,1,1,1). At q=(1,0,0,0,0,1), the printed two binomials vanish and the necessary third binomial equals 1.
independent_verification.counterevidence: A localization or saturation interpretation would exclude points but is not the stated affine equality. The general lattice-count and area identities are exactly correct; the prior 49 finite checks were inspected and the symbolic identity independently recomputed.
independent_verification.impact: Retain Minor because the source expressly says on p.27 that this example is not used subsequently; no central dependency was established.
independent_verification.repair_check: Only necessity of the missing binomial is proved; sufficiency of an amended ideal and the full symplectic example are not certified.

findings.title: Proper onto image does not guarantee all-time gradient flow
findings.decisive_evidence: X=C\{-1}, π inclusion, trivial S1 action, ψ=0, Z empty; map proper onto image but φ_t(0)=-t exits at t=1.
findings.alternative: Fails stronger full-target properness required by GH4II, so not a counterexample to Theorem 3.7.
findings.impact: Standalone completeness lemma overstated; core theorem not refuted by this example
findings.repair_status: Full-target properness excludes example; whole revised lemma not proved

independent_verification.source_scope: PDF p.44 Lemma A.1, p.12 (GH4)II-III, p.45 use in A.3; Section 3.2 notation.
independent_verification.hypotheses: The standalone lemma restates a morphism of varieties, not the full degeneration assumptions imposed later in Appendix A. C minus {-1} is a smooth affine variety, pi is regular, Z is empty, U0={0}, and the restricted Euclidean form is Kahler. Trivial S1 is a connected Hamiltonian action with moment map zero preserving metric and fibers. The map to its image is a homeomorphism and hence proper there. Additional condition (iii) is not needed for the first all-time conclusion.
independent_verification.decisive_check: The normalized negative gradient trajectory starting at 0 is -t, with derivative -1; at t=1 it reaches the removed point. Its explicit solution establishes finite-time escape.
independent_verification.counterevidence: This example is not proper into the full target and is excluded by (GH4)II. In the theorem application, (GH4)III saturation also prevents a fixed-moment trajectory from leaving its assigned subfamily. The appendix's location is not the reason for Minor.
independent_verification.impact: Retain Minor for the standalone overstatement because its counterexample does not invalidate the stronger hypotheses actually supplied in the core application.
independent_verification.repair_check: Full-target properness excludes this escape; no complete replacement lemma is claimed.

findings.title: Strong convexity criterion loses zero-weight exception
findings.decisive_evidence: E=C0⊕C1; µ=|z1|²/2 has pointed image [0,∞) and unbounded zero fiber.
findings.alternative: Earlier nonnegative-combination criterion is correct; later application excludes zero weights.
findings.impact: Local equivalence false; cited downstream properness not refuted
findings.repair_status: Pointed cone plus all weights nonzero criterion analytically proved

independent_verification.source_scope: PDF p.7 Lemma 2.2(ii), pp.22-23 Lemma 4.10 proof.
independent_verification.hypotheses: The lemma permits zero weights. The unitary representation C0 plus C1 is finite dimensional with the required normalized quadratic moment map.
independent_verification.decisive_check: The moment image is the pointed ray, while (n,0) is an unbounded sequence in the zero fiber. Independent symbolic limit confirms the stated unbounded witness; the properness conclusion is analytic.
independent_verification.counterevidence: The earlier nonnegative-zero-combination criterion correctly rejects the example. The later Lemma 4.10 proves zero is not a weight, so its properness application is not refuted.
independent_verification.impact: Retain Minor for the final equivalence only; no core damage follows from this witness.
independent_verification.repair_check: Rechecked the full finite-weight repair analytically: pointedness supplies a strictly positive functional on all nonzero generators; its minimum bounds the squared norm on inverse images of compact sets. Zero weights or a nontrivial nonnegative zero relation give an unbounded zero fiber.

independent_acceptance_scope: The five existing Problems only. Initial findings and their severities are confirmed; no scientific report correction was required.
